Team — quick technical summary from runtime side after initial triage:

Findings:
- The v3q quant profile introduced a different kernel path for decoder-attention and a small change in KV cache key layout (metadata tag). This is intended and was visible in synthetic tests, but in FastPay's workload the token distribution and short-prompt heavy tail caused frequent KV thrash.
- KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x for active shards (see attached quant_profile-v3q.patch for diffs we used to reproduce locally). Misses lead to repeated recomputation and forced more heavy kernel launches (higher latency) and contention, which can also trigger 500s in their tight threadpool.

Immediate mitigations we can apply from our side:
1) Fallback routing: route FastPay's traffic to the previous non-quantized variant (v3-fp16) while we patch v3q. This is the fastest remediation.
2) Canary rollback: perform a weighted rollback to 0% v3q within their region and autorebalance.
3) Kernel backstop: force the runtime to use the older attention kernel for affected shard sizes (temporary, requires restart of serving nodes).

Risks: fallback adds unit-cost delta but reduces customer impact immediately. Kernel backstop will require a short restart window (~2–4 minutes) per pool.

I'll prepare the patch and playbook. Vivek — can you confirm capacity for routing change + short restarts? Monica — help me coordinate the canary windows with their ops.

— Markus
Engineering Director, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — final update & exec summary for FastPay leadership: 

What happened (brief): after enabling quantization profile v3q for redwood-model-v3, FastPay's production traffic saw an unexpected increase in KV cache miss rate. The miss pattern is workload-specific (short prompts + skewed token distribution) which caused increased recomputation and tail kernel contention, manifesting as p95 latency spike and intermittent 500s.

Immediate actions taken (done):
- Traffic rolled back to v3-fp16 for FastPay (routing flag pushed) at 03:12 PT on 2026-02-17 — p95 returned to baseline in ~18m.
- Threadpool scaled +20% while cache warmed to reduce 500s.
- Kernel backstop patch staged for non-quant attention path; restart window scheduled and executed with no customer-visible downtime.
- JIRA INF-4823 opened; canary-playbook.md and patch attached to the ticket.

Next steps (short-term):
- Engineering will harden v3q for short-prompt workloads (work on kernel selection heuristics + KV key compatibility). Target: low-risk patch and validated canary by 2026-02-24.
- We'll provide a formal postmortem to FastPay with timelines for any further mitigations and a proposed SLA credit calculation.

Ask of FastPay: please confirm if you'd like us to perform a blue/green test with a small percentage of traffic on your staging cluster before any re-introduction of v3q. Also share any high-priority time windows when rolling restarts are disallowed.

Attachments: canary-playbook.md (playbook, 6KB)

I'll follow up with a short slide for your execs and coordinate a sync if you'd like. Sorry again for the impact — we take this seriously.
